metadata.description: A state-of-the-art, deeply structured AI Engineering Body of Knowledge. It bridges foundational ML with modern GenAI/Agentic ecosystems, breaking down complex architectures into 5-level hierarchies with practical insights for building systems from scratch.
metadata.methodology: Topics investigated to 5 sub-levels (Domain -> System -> Component -> Mechanism -> Algorithm/Technique) with explicit 'from-scratch' implementation guidance.

modern_ai_ecosystem_tools.note: Curated SOTA tooling landscape for the modern AI engineer.

deep_dive_systems_architecture.note: 5-level deep investigations into core AI systems, focusing on practical implementation from scratch.

systems.description: Building a production-grade RAG system beyond naive semantic search.
systems.level_5_practical_insight: Build from scratch: Use OpenCV to detect bounding boxes of text/images, pass cropped regions to a lightweight VLM (like Florence-2) to generate text summaries, and stitch them back into a hierarchical JSON tree preserving document structure.

systems.level_2_component: Fusion of Sparse and Dense Retrieval
systems.level_5_practical_insight: Build from scratch: Execute BM25 (via rank_bm25 library) and HNSW vector search in parallel. Take top-K from both, compute RRF scores without normalizing the underlying values, and return the fused top-N. Bypasses the need to calibrate different scoring scales.

systems.level_4_algorithm: Conditional Edge Routing based on LLM Structured Output
systems.level_5_practical_insight: Build from scratch: Define agent state as a Pydantic schema. Use an LLM with structured output to return a 'next_node' string. Implement a graph router using Python dictionaries where {current_node: {condition: next_node}}. Force the LLM to output valid tool arguments using JSON schema enforcement before adding the tool call to the message history.

systems.description: Optimizing LLM deployment for high throughput.
systems.level_5_practical_insight: Build from scratch: Maintain a Python asyncio queue of incoming requests. Instead of static batches, at each forward pass, pull available requests, pad them to max_seq_len_in_batch, and compute. Post-forward, strip padding, return tokens to respective clients, and immediately inject a new request into the vacated slot without waiting for the batch to finish.

systems.description: Building custom vector search for scale.
systems.level_5_practical_insight: Build from scratch: Create a multi-layer graph using Python dictionaries. Insert vectors layer-by-layer (probabilistic). For search, start at the top layer, greedily move to the closest neighbor until local minimum, drop a layer, repeat. Use `heapq` to maintain candidate and dynamic nearest-neighbor lists.

systems.description: Building standardized interfaces for LLM tool use.
systems.level_5_practical_insight: Build from scratch: Create a Python `httpserver` or asyncio stdin/stdout reader. Parse incoming JSON-RPC requests, map the 'method' string (e.g., 'tools/call') to internal Python functions using a registry decorator, execute the function, and wrap the result in a standardized JSON-RPC response envelope.

systems.description: Aligning base models to specific instructions.
systems.level_5_practical_insight: Build from scratch: Use PyTorch to freeze the base model weights. For a target nn.Linear layer (W), initialize two new matrices A (rank x features) and B (out x rank) with Gaussian and zero weights respectively. Compute output as `base_output + (B(A(input))) * (1/rank)`. Only A and B require gradients.

Build from scratch: After every N agent turns, prompt an LLM to extract (S, P, O) triples from the conversation. Store these in a `networkx` graph object. When a new user query arrives, run a graph traversal (e.g., BFS) starting from nodes mentioned in the query to pull in relevant historical context dynamically.
